card.name: Words before his/their/himself in narrative
card.fires_on: Verbs or small linking words in narrative prose right before a reflexive or possessive pronoun such as himself, themselves, his or their. The pole fires on the word just ahead of that pronoun.

modes.label: Verb before reflexive
modes.description: A verb that is followed by himself or themselves.
modes.example: who called himself the "New Haman", organized attacks on the Jews, who<< defended>> themselves.

modes.label: Word before possessive
modes.description: A small word or verb that is followed by his or their and a noun.
modes.example: from such works that Egyptian liberals drew many<< of>> their ideas.

modes.label: Preposition before itself/himself
modes.description: A preposition that is followed by a reflexive pronoun.
modes.example: he became tempted to keep it<< for>> himself.

card.writes: It lowers the chance of you/your and favors third-person continuations, which fits a reflexive or possessive pronoun about someone else.
card.plain: It fires on the word just before a pronoun like himself or their that refers back to the person being described.
